BAFTA winning writer to return to Rhyl Pavilion Theatre

2 hrs ago
Entertainment
By Josh Price Reporter

Share

0 comments
0:00 / 0:00

Comedy fans are in for a treat as a BAFTA-winning writer and actor brings a night of laughter and nostalgia to the stage.

Phil Mealey, best known as the co-creator and star of the cult BBC sitcom Early Doors, will appear at Rhyl Pavilion Theatre on Friday, 13 November 2026, for A Celebration of Early Doors: Behind the Bar and Beyond.

The show promises a behind-the-scenes look at the much-loved comedy set in The Grapes pub, featuring untold stories, clips, and live music from the series, performed by Mealey himself.

Mr Mealey said: "It’s a chance to step back into that world again – the people, the pub, the music, the laughs – and share the stories behind it all."

Fans can expect previously unseen moments, stories from the making of the show, and rare insights into how the series came to life.

Early Doors, co-written by Mealey and Craig Cash, ran for two seasons on the BBC and featured a cast including John Henshaw, Maxine Peake, James McAvoy, and Lee Ingleby.

Mealey later wrote for The Royle Family, earning a BAFTA for Best Situation Comedy.

Together with Cash, he also created Sunshine, starring Steve Coogan and Bernard Hill, and Broken Biscuits, featuring Alun Armstrong and Alison Steadman.

Rhyl Pavilion Theatre, a 1,031-seat venue on the North Wales coast, regularly hosts major acts and touring productions.

Recent shows at the theatre have included Chicago, Mrs Brown’s Boys, and performances by John Bishop.

Read More:

  • Cast announced for this year's pantomime at Rhyl Pavilion Theatre

  • Glenn Miller & Big Band Spectacular heading to Rhyl Pavilion Theatre

A Celebration of Early Doors begins at 7.30pm.

Tickets are priced at £34.95 and are available to book through the Rhyl Pavilion Theatre website at rhylpavilion.co.uk.
